transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… my head’s just been kind of foggy. I’ve been making small mistakes in my client notes and forgetting what I was about to do. That’s not really like me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I guess I have. Most mornings I wake up with this kind of heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through work and talk to people, but inside I just feel… sad, kind of flat.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual or finding it harder to get through the day?

Yeah… I’ve been more worn out than usual. Even if I haven’t done much, my body feels tired. Little things at work, like helping someone shower, or just carrying groceries… they take more out of me than they should.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things that usually make you happy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I haven’t really been paying close attention to that. I still do things if I’m supposed to, but I guess they don’t feel like much lately.
Have you completely lost interest in doing things you used to enjoy, or do you still find some pleasure in them, even if it's less than before?
I wouldn’t say completely. It’s more like… I can still get a little something out of things sometimes, but it feels muted. Not like it used to.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Probably about a month… maybe a little more. It’s just been this low, foggy kind of feeling hanging around.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?
Yeah… a little. I keep thinking about my tío, before he passed. Like I should’ve called more, or gone to see him sooner. I know I can’t change it, but it feels like I failed him, you know… as family.
Would you say that you’re no longer getting any pleasure out of things you used to enjoy, or is there still some enjoyment, even if it’s less than before?
Like I said, not none… I guess there’s still a little enjoyment sometimes. Just not much.
Can you think of a specific time recently when you felt any pleasure or happiness doing something you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… not a specific time, really. Maybe something small here or there, but nothing that stands out.
Would you say that you’ve lost almost all pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or is there still some pleasure, even if it’s much less than before?
I don’t think it’s almost all gone. It’s just… less. A lot less sometimes, but not completely gone.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most things you used to care about, or do you still try to do them even if they don’t feel as good as before?
I still try sometimes, I guess. It just doesn’t feel like it used to, so I don’t always stick with it.
Would you say that you’re barely able to feel any pleasure at all anymore, even in things you used to really enjoy?
I don’t think it’s that extreme. I can still feel something sometimes… just not as much, I guess.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough almost every day, even when there’s no real reason for it?
Yeah… I guess so. I keep thinking about my tío before he passed, like I should’ve called more or gone to see him sooner. It just sits there, like I failed him somehow.
Have you had days where you didn’t feel any pleasure at all in anything, even things you used to really enjoy?
I’m not sure… I mean, maybe some days feel pretty flat, but I don’t think I’d say absolutely nothing gives me any pleasure. It’s more like it’s muted.
Have there been days recently when nothing at all—absolutely nothing—gave you any pleasure, even things you used to really enjoy?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say absolutely nothing. Some things still get through a little, just not like before.
Would you say that most of the time, you’re not really getting any pleasure out of things you used to enjoy, even a little bit?
I don’t think it’s most of the time, no. It’s just… some things feel kind of dulled down, but not gone completely.

Would you say that the pleasure you get from things you used to enjoy is only a little less than before, or has it dropped to the point where you're hardly feeling any pleasure at all most of the time?
It’s probably just a little less. I mean, I still feel something from things… it’s just not as much as before, I guess.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in almost everything you used to care about, so that even doing things you normally enjoy feels like a chore most days?
No… I wouldn’t say almost everything. Some things are harder to get into, but it’s not like everything feels like a chore most days.
Would you say that most days, you’re not interested in doing even the things you normally enjoy, like it’s hard to get motivated for almost anything?
Not most days, no. I can still get interested in things… maybe it takes a little more effort sometimes, but it’s not like I’m unmotivated for almost everything.

inference_history.note: The patient continues to endorse symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia (diminished pleasure, not completely lost), fatigue, and self-blame. The duration is over one month, suggesting a sustained mood disturbance. The severity remains unclear, hence all subtypes of major depressive disorder (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2) remain possible. F32.3 (with psychotic features) is ruled out as there is no evidence of delusions or hallucinations. F32.8 and F32.9 are retained due to possible atypical or unspecified presentations.

The patient continues to endorse symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia (diminished pleasure, not nearly complete loss), fatigue, and excessive guilt. These symptoms align with moderate to severe depressive episodes (F32.1-F32.2) or other specified/ unspecified depressive disorders. No new information sufficiently narrows the differential to a single code or rules out any specific candidate definitively.

F32.2 (Major depressive disorder, severe) has been ruled out due to the patient not endorsing near-complete loss of pleasure or interest, and no indication of severe functional impairment. The patient continues to report a persistent low mood, reduced interest/pleasure most of the time but not completely absent, fatigue, and guilt, consistent with mild to moderate depression.
